text:
eli.h: heads-up: discovered a flaky case in the Go SDK generator stream when cancelling via context (from a sample app). sometimes it cleanly stops, sometimes we get a trailing token and a goroutine leak. pprof shows the runtime waiting in a write.

nora.p: ouch. can you paste the smallest repro?

eli.h: minimal loop we ship in the sample:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
for {
  chunk, err := stream.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { return err }
  fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
```
If the timeout fires we cancel the ctx. Most of the time Recv returns with context.Canceled or EOF. Sometimes it prints one more chunk then the process hangs and two goroutines are left blocked.

rashid.r: i think this is the same class of bug we saw with other languages: auth token refresh sends a keepalive/write and the cancel races with that write. The runtime wakes the socket and appends a fragment from the retry path, so the client sees inconsistent tail output.

nora.p: yes. SDK-level invariants should be: 1) Recv must not return a non-nil chunk when there's an error, 2) cancellation must be observable immediately. otherwise apps get partial/duplicated outputs and leaks.

eli.h: I hacked a local workaround: wrap Recv in a select on ctx.Done and call CloseWithError (not currently in SDK, so used Close + sentinel)
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
    _ = stream.Close() // best-effort to unblock
    return ctx.Err()
  default:
  }
  chunk, err := stream.Recv()
  // handle
}
```
This reduced leaks but didn't eliminate cases where Recv returned a nil chunk after Close.

rashid.r: runtime change: expose Stream.CloseWithError(err error) and make Recv guarantee: if err != nil then chunk == nil. Also make CloseWithError idempotent and safe for signal handlers. That lets clients do: CloseWithError(context.Canceled) and Recv returns context.Canceled immediately.

nora.p: second runtime change: disable automatic auth refresh/retry for long-lived generator streams. If a 401 happens mid-stream we should surface a distinct error instead of replaying a retry that can append tokens. Document that streaming endpoints are non-retriable.

eli.h: also add a small quickstart snippet for CLI apps showing signal.NotifyContext and CloseWithError pattern, plus a tiny integration test that runs with -race and checks for goroutine leaks via pprof.

runtime-bot: note: filed issue runtime#612 (WIP) to implement CloseWithError and streaming retry policy.

rashid.r: one more DX thing: update the Go SDK README with a short "Why my generator kept running after Ctrl-C" troubleshooting blurb. People hit this in onboarding and immediately open issues.

nora.p: agreed. impl plan:
- SDK: add Stream.CloseWithError(err error) + unit tests for idempotency
- Runtime: ensure Recv semantics and stop mid-stream auth retries
- Samples: add CLI + web quickstart snippets showing cancellation pattern
- Docs: quick paragraph in onboarding + console troubleshooting note

eli.h: I'll open the PR for the sample and the README blurb (link forthcoming). thanks all. :pray:
